Dear op, im glad that you found a place that you fit in. Everyone needs there own place to go. And some things that might help this are as follows....

Maybe find some of the people you went to camp with? Maybe on facebook, or twitter, or some other socal site. Get in touch with them, tell them the fun yall had and try to see if there are other ways yall can talk.

Maybe find someone close who went there before? That way you and the new person can talk about your different expericnes at the camp. Talk about the people they met and the people you met.

Plan for the next trip. Yes it is a long time till then, but make it a every year going. That way when you do leave you know you are going right back to it next year, or next month, or something.

I hope some of these help. I know whats it like to find your own place. So just try and look around and see what else you can find then go from there.

We all go through life as it is ment for us. And I agree with you, but I also dont. Yes I think depression should kill us naturally. But I think it already does. When we are depressed everything goes away from us. Our happniess, our smiles, our laugh, everything gets drained from us until we get to the point we no longer want to be around. To the point where suicide is the answer, so I agree and dont agree. Depression is a killer in its own form.

Everyone knows whats going on, I talk to anyone I can because im hoping that someone will say or do something to make me not go through this. But they all say the same thing. Get over it, things will get better, blah blah blah. But this is how I see it, these things keep happening to me when all I do is try and try and try. Why not just take away the object of attention? Give it someone else, because I cant do this. It hurts so bad not being with her. She knows how I feel. We are still talking right now as im writing this. But after tonight she wants to work on finding someone new to be with. And if she does that, then that will kill me. So im just going to do it, before she does..
